title: Assessing and Treating Burns: Depth, Size, Cooling, Fluids

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already cool burns, cover them, give oxygen and keep the patient warm. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Judge a burn's depth, size and severity quickly
  2. Cool and dress it the BC way
  3. Know when the PCP gives fluids, and where the Parkland formula fits

Textbook: Chapter 23, PDF pages 1932–1969
slides.say: Welcome back to burns. Today is about the patient in front of you. As EMRs, you already cool burns, cover them, give oxygen, and keep patients warm. As a PCP, two things change. First, your assessment must produce numbers: how deep, how big, how serious. Those numbers decide where the patient goes and whether the fluid protocol starts. Second, you now control the IV. So today: depth, size, and severity; cooling the BC way; and when the PCP gives fluids, including the textbook's Parkland formula.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回到烧伤这一章。今天讲你面前的病人。作为 EMR，你们已经会冷却创面、覆盖伤口、给氧、保暖。作为 PCP，有两点变了。第一，你的评估要得出数字：多深、多大、多严重。这些数字决定病人去哪家医院，也决定要不要启动补液流程。第二，静脉通路现在由你掌控。所以今天讲：深度、面积和严重程度；按 BC 的方法冷却；PCP 什么时候补液，包括教材里的 Parkland 公式。

slides.title: Stop the burning, then look wider
slides.body:
1. Stop, drop, roll; or smother with a blanket
  2. Remove smouldering clothes, rings, watches, zippers
  3. Cut around stuck fabric; leave melted material
  • Walking and talking? Can still be critical
  • Combative = hypoxic until proven otherwise
  • Burns alone don't cause coma → look for other injury or toxins
slides.say: First, stop the burning. A person on fire shouldn't run: stop, drop, and roll, or lay them down and smother the flames with a blanket. Remove smouldering clothing and anything that holds heat, like rings, watches, and zippers. A burned hand swells, and a ring can become a tourniquet. If cloth is stuck to the skin, cut around it, and leave melted material for the hospital. Then look wider. A critically burned patient may walk up and say, I'm cold. A combative patient is hypoxic until proven otherwise. And burns alone don't cause unconsciousness, so look for a head injury or toxic smoke.
slides.sayZh: 第一步，停止烧伤。身上着火的人不能跑：停下、躺倒、打滚，或者让他躺下，用毯子把火捂灭。去掉闷燃的衣物和一切蓄热的东西，比如戒指、手表、拉链。烧伤的手会肿，戒指可能变成止血带。布料粘在皮肤上就沿周围剪开，熔进皮肉的东西留给医院处理。然后放宽视野。伤得很重的病人可能自己走过来，只说一句「我好冷」。躁动的病人在排除之前都当作缺氧。单纯烧伤不会让人昏迷，所以要找颅脑外伤或有毒烟雾。

slides.title: The airway: four groups
slides.body:
Crashing nowarrest, or swelling you can seeairway now; plan for failure
Getting worseburns plus toxic smokebest handled in hospital if possible
At riskopen now, risky historycool humid O₂; report the history
No riskno distressoxygen anyway
slides.say: The book sorts burn airways into four groups. Group one is crashing now: in arrest, or with swelling you can see getting worse. That airway must be secured immediately, with a backup plan if it fails. Group two is getting worse, for example burns plus toxic smoke; if at all possible, that airway is better handled in hospital. Group three has an open airway but a risky story: give cool, humidified oxygen if you can, and make sure the hospital hears the history. Group four has no risk, but still gets oxygen. Your skill is placing the patient in the right group early.
slides.sayZh: 书里把烧伤病人的气道分成四组。第一组正在崩溃：心跳呼吸骤停，或者眼看着肿起来。这种气道必须马上处理，还要备好失败时的预案。第二组在恶化，比如烧伤加有毒烟雾；能等的话，这种气道最好交给医院处理。第三组气道现在通畅，但病史有风险：能的话给凉的湿化氧，并确保医院知道这段病史。第四组没有风险，但照样给氧。你的本事在于尽早把病人放进正确的那一组。

slides.title: How deep is the burn?
slides.body:
Superficialepidermis only; red, blanches, painfulheals in 3–7 days
Partial-thicknessinto the dermis; blisters, wet, very painfuldeep ones look like full
Full-thicknessall layers; white, leathery or charredno refill; numb centre

Zones: dead centre (coagulation) → stasis (can be saved, or lost in 24–48 h) → hyperemia (recovers).
slides.say: Next, depth. A superficial burn involves only the epidermis, the top layer: red, blanching, painful, usually no blisters. A partial-thickness burn reaches the dermis: blisters, a wet look, and severe pain. A full-thickness burn destroys all the skin layers: white, leathery, or charred, with no capillary refill, often numb in the centre but painful at the edges. Each burn also has zones. The dead centre is the zone of coagulation. Around it is the zone of stasis, with poor blood flow. It can recover, or die within twenty-four to forty-eight hours if perfusion is poor. That's one reason your oxygen and fluids matter.
slides.sayZh: 接下来看深度。浅表烧伤只伤到表皮，也就是最外层：发红、按压褪色、疼痛，通常没有水疱。部分层烧伤伤到真皮：有水疱、看起来湿、剧痛。全层烧伤毁掉皮肤所有层：发白、皮革样或焦黑，没有毛细血管充盈，中心常常不痛，边缘却痛。每处烧伤还分区。中心坏死的是凝固区；它周围是淤滞区，血流差，可能恢复，也可能在灌注不好时于二十四到四十八小时内坏死。这正是你给氧和补液重要的原因之一。

slides.title: How big is the burn?
slides.body:
Adult areaRule of nines
Head and neck9%
Each arm9%
Front of trunk; back of trunk18% each
Each leg18%
Genitals1%
  • Count only partial- and full-thickness; skip superficial
  • Book's rule of palms: palm, no fingers ≈ 1%
  • Newer sources (CNS 8.4): palm alone ≈ 0.5%, palm + fingers ≈ 1%; exam: no number
slides.say: Now size, as a percentage of total body surface area. In an adult, the rule of nines gives the head nine percent, each arm nine, the front of the trunk eighteen, the back eighteen, each leg eighteen, and the genitals one. Children have a bigger head and smaller legs, so use the child chart. For small or patchy burns, the book uses the rule of palms: the patient's own palm, without the fingers, is about one percent. Newer sources, like your school's reading, say the palm alone is about half a percent, and the palm with fingers about one percent; the exam gives no number. Count only partial- and full-thickness burns; red, superficial skin doesn't count. Your estimate guides the destination, and in BC it decides whether the hypovolemia protocol applies.
slides.sayZh: 再看面积，用占全身体表面积的百分比表示。成人用九分法：头颈百分之九，每只手臂九，躯干前面十八，后面十八，每条腿十八，会阴生殖器一。儿童头大腿小，要用儿童的图表。小面积或零散的烧伤，书里用手掌法：病人自己的手掌（不含手指）约等于百分之一。较新的资料，比如学校的读物，说单是手掌约占百分之零点五，手掌连同手指约占百分之一；考纲没有给数字。只算部分层和全层烧伤，发红的浅表烧伤不算。你的估算决定送往哪里，在 BC 还决定是否适用低血容量流程。

slides.q: An adult has partial-thickness burns over the whole front of the trunk and the whole right arm. His back is red like a sunburn, with no blisters. What is the burn size, and what does it mean for you as a PCP?
options: 18%: under 20%, so not a hypovolemia-protocol burn yet
27%: over 20% BSA, so the BC hypovolemia protocol applies
27%, but the BC hypovolemia protocol needs a systolic under 90 first
slides.say: Let's practise. An adult has partial-thickness burns over the whole front of the trunk and the whole right arm. His back is red like a sunburn, with no blisters. What is the burn size, and what does it mean for you as a PCP? A, eighteen percent: under twenty percent, so not a hypovolemia protocol burn yet. B, twenty-seven percent: over twenty percent body surface area, so the BC hypovolemia protocol applies. C, forty-five percent: the red back counts too. D, twenty-seven percent, but the BC hypovolemia protocol needs a systolic under ninety first. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来练一下。一名成人躯干前面全部和整条右臂是部分层烧伤，背部像晒伤一样发红、没有水疱。烧伤面积是多少？对你这个 PCP 意味着什么？A 百分之十八，不到百分之二十，还不算低血容量流程里的烧伤；B 百分之二十七，超过体表面积百分之二十，适用 BC 低血容量流程；C 百分之四十五，发红的背部也要算；D 百分之二十七，但 BC 低血容量流程要等收缩压低于九十才能启动。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The front of the trunk is eighteen percent and one arm is nine, so twenty-seven percent. The red back is superficial, so it doesn't count. Burns over twenty percent of body surface area, partial and full thickness, are listed in the BC hypovolemia protocol, so as a PCP you plan vascular access en route, and a bolus if he becomes hypotensive or poorly perfused. A forgets the arm. C wrongly counts a superficial burn. D is wrong: these burns are listed in the protocol, and BC lets you start it above a systolic of ninety when the extent of the injuries makes shock likely.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。躯干前面百分之十八，一只手臂百分之九，合计百分之二十七。发红的背部是浅表烧伤，不算。部分层加全层烧伤超过体表面积百分之二十，就列在 BC 低血容量流程里，所以作为 PCP，你要计划在途中开静脉通路；如果他出现低血压或灌注不良，再推注补液。A 漏算了手臂。C 错把浅表烧伤算进去。D 错在这类烧伤本身就列在流程里，而且当损伤范围让休克很可能发生时，BC 允许收缩压高于九十也启动这个流程。

slides.title: Which burns need a burn centre?
slides.body:
• Partial-thickness > 10%; any full-thickness
  • Face, hands, feet, genitals, perineum, major joints
  • Electrical (incl. lightning), chemical, inhalation
  • Serious illness, like COPD or heart disease
  • Major trauma too → trauma destination rules come first
  • Circumferential burns: neck, chest, limbs → check pulses often
slides.say: Severity decides the destination. The book's burn centre criteria include partial-thickness burns over ten percent and any full-thickness burn. Location matters as much as size: the face, hands, feet, genitals, perineum, and major joints all qualify. So do electrical burns, including lightning, chemical burns, inhalation injuries, and patients with serious illness like COPD or heart disease. If there's also major trauma, trauma destination rules come first. And look for circumferential burns, which go all the way around a body part. As they swell, they act like a tourniquet, threatening the airway, the breathing, or a limb's circulation.
slides.sayZh: 严重程度决定去哪家医院。书里转烧伤中心的标准包括：部分层烧伤超过百分之十，以及任何全层烧伤。部位和面积同样重要：面部、手、脚、生殖器、会阴和大关节，都符合。电烧伤（包括雷击）、化学烧伤、吸入性损伤，以及有 COPD、心脏病等严重疾病的病人，也都符合。如果同时有严重创伤，创伤分流规则优先。还要找环形烧伤，也就是绕身体某部位一整圈的烧伤。它们肿起来就像止血带，会威胁气道、呼吸或肢体循环。

slides.title: Cooling: the exam rule
slides.body:
Exam: cool for 15–20 minutes

  • Cool, not cold, running water; bystander cooling counts
  • Cooling is also pain relief
  • No ice; no creams, ointments or sprays
  • Then sterile, non-stick, dry gauze
  • Don't pop blisters; keep the patient warm

Must go now? Cool saline may be enough. No immediate threat? Staying over 20 min for running water is OK. BCEHS H10: cool 15 min; gel burn dressings.
slides.say: The BC exam guidelines are very specific about cooling, for every licence level. Cool the burn for fifteen to twenty minutes, including any good cooling bystanders already did. Use cool, not cold, running water; cooling is also pain relief. With no immediate life threat, it's acceptable to stay on scene more than twenty minutes to reach running water. If the patient must go now, cool saline may be enough. Never use ice, creams, or sprays. Then cover with sterile, non-stick, dry gauze. Leave blisters intact. And fight the cold with blankets and a warm ambulance. BCEHS cools for fifteen minutes, then uses gel burn dressings.
slides.sayZh: BC 考纲对冷却规定得很具体，适用于所有执照级别。冷却烧伤十五到二十分钟，旁人已经做过的有效冷却也算在内。用凉而不冰的流动水；冷却本身也是镇痛。没有立即致命的威胁时，为了用上流动水，在现场停留超过二十分钟是可以的。病人必须马上走的话，用凉的生理盐水也许就够了。绝不用冰、药膏或喷剂。然后用无菌、不粘、干的纱布覆盖。水疱保持完整。再用毯子和暖和的救护车对抗寒冷。BCEHS 是冷却十五分钟，然后用凝胶烧伤敷料。

slides.title: The Parkland formula (textbook)
slides.body:
2–4 mL × kg × % TBSA = first 24 h

  • Half in the first 8 h, counted from the injury
  • Example: 80 kg, 25% → 4,000–8,000 mL in 24 h
  • First 8 h: 2,000–4,000 mL (250–500 mL/h)
  • Reached 2 h after injury? First half over the next 6 h

A hospital planning tool, not a BC rule. Too much fluid ("fluid creep") harms too.
slides.say: The textbook teaches the Parkland formula. It estimates fluid for the first twenty-four hours: two to four millilitres, times body weight in kilograms, times the percent of body surface burned. Half goes in during the first eight hours, counted from the injury, not from when you arrive. So an eighty-kilogram patient with twenty-five percent burns needs four to eight litres in a day, two to four litres in the first eight hours. Reach them two hours after the injury, and that first half goes in over six hours. It's a hospital tool, not a BC rule, and too much fluid, called fluid creep, causes harmful swelling.
slides.sayZh: 教材讲的是 Parkland 公式，用来估算伤后头二十四小时的补液量：两到四毫升，乘以体重公斤数，再乘以烧伤面积百分比。其中一半要在头八小时内输完，从受伤时刻算起，不是从你到达算起。所以八十公斤、烧伤百分之二十五的病人，一天需要四到八升，头八小时两到四升。如果你在伤后两小时才接手，这前一半就要在剩下的六小时里输完。它是医院的工具，不是 BC 规则；补液过多，叫「液体蠕变」，会造成有害的水肿。

slides.q: Bystanders cooled a child's scalded forearm under the tap for 10 minutes before you arrived. She is stable and the burn is small. What should you do next?
options: Cool 5–10 more minutes, then a dry, sterile, non-stick dressing; keep her warm
Switch to an ice pack for 20 minutes
Cool for 45 more minutes to be safe
slides.say: Here's a cooling question. Bystanders cooled a child's scalded forearm under the tap for ten minutes before you arrived. She is stable and the burn is small. What should you do next? A, stop cooling: ten minutes is enough. B, cool five to ten more minutes, then a dry, sterile, non-stick dressing, and keep her warm. C, switch to an ice pack for twenty minutes. D, cool for forty-five more minutes to be safe. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 一道冷却题。你到达前，旁人已经在水龙头下给一个孩子烫伤的前臂冲了十分钟。孩子情况稳定，烧伤面积小。下一步怎么做？A 停止冷却，十分钟够了；B 再冲五到十分钟，然后盖干的、无菌、不粘的敷料，并给她保暖；C 改用冰袋敷二十分钟；D 为保险再冲四十五分钟。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The BC exam guidelines recommend fifteen to twenty minutes of cooling in total, including effective cooling by bystanders, so five to ten more minutes brings her into that range. Then dress the burn with sterile, non-stick, dry gauze, and keep her warm. A stops too early. C is wrong because ice should never be used on a burn. D goes far past the exam time and risks making a child hypothermic.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 考纲建议总共冷却十五到二十分钟，旁人做的有效冷却也算在内，所以再冲五到十分钟正好达到这个范围。然后用无菌、不粘、干的纱布包扎，并给她保暖。A 停得太早。C 错，烧伤绝不能用冰。D 远远超过考纲的时间，可能让孩子体温过低。

slides.title: Pain relief for burns
slides.body:
BC optionBurn watch-out
CoolingBC counts it as pain relief
Entonoxburn pain is an indication; not with inhalation injury
Methoxyflurane18+, alert, stable; not with decreased LOC
AcetaminophenPO; IV route (50 kg+) needs an IV
Ibuprofennot with anticoagulants, GI bleed, pregnancy

The book's morphine and fentanyl are not on the BC licensing exam (in BCEHS: ACP drugs).
slides.say: The BC burn protocol says to consider pain management. Cooling itself counts as pain relief. Entonox lists burn pain as an indication, but it's contraindicated with an inhalation injury, so check the airway story first. Methoxyflurane is for alert, stable adults eighteen or older. Acetaminophen can go by mouth, and its IV route, for patients fifty kilograms or more, needs an IV, which only a PCP can start. Ibuprofen is out with blood thinners, a stomach bleed, or pregnancy. Score the pain before and after, using the same scale. The book's morphine and fentanyl aren't on the BC licensing exam, and in BCEHS they're ACP drugs.
slides.sayZh: BC 烧伤流程说要考虑镇痛。冷却本身就算镇痛。笑气把烧伤疼痛列为适应证，但有吸入性损伤时禁用，所以先查清气道情况。甲氧氟烷用于清醒、稳定、十八岁及以上的成人。对乙酰氨基酚可以口服；它的静脉给药途径用于五十公斤及以上的病人，需要静脉通路，而只有 PCP 能开。用抗凝药、有消化道出血或怀孕时不能用布洛芬。给药前后都要评分，用同一个量表。书里的吗啡和芬太尼执照考试不考，在 BCEHS 是 ACP 用药。

slides.title: Chemical burns: flush long, eyes too
slides.body:
• Lots of water, right away; strip clothes, shoes and socks
  • Book: flush about 30 min before moving; strong alkali 1–2 h
  • Keep flushing en route if needed; keep the patient warm after
  • Don't hunt for antidotes; unknown chemical → just water
  • Eyes: water only, lids open, protect the other eye
  • Contact lenses: pause after 1–2 min to remove them

BCEHS J01: flush at least 15 min. Exam burn protocol: cool 15–20 min.
slides.say: Here's how long to flush chemical burns. Start immediately with plenty of water, and strip off clothing, including shoes and socks, without contaminating yourself. Don't hunt for antidotes; water works. The book says flush for about thirty minutes before moving the patient, and one to two hours for strong alkalis like oven or drain cleaner, though you can keep flushing during transport. BCEHS says flush for at least fifteen minutes, and the exam's burn protocol cools for fifteen to twenty. Afterwards, keep the patient warm. For the eyes, use water only, never vinegar or baking soda. Hold the lids open, and keep the runoff away from the other eye. If contact lenses don't wash out, pause after a minute or two to remove them.
slides.sayZh: 化学烧伤要冲多久？马上用大量清水冲，同时脱掉衣服，包括鞋袜，别让自己沾上。不要找解毒剂，清水就有效。书上说，搬动病人前最好冲大约三十分钟；烤箱清洁剂、管道疏通剂这类强碱要冲一到两小时，转运途中可以继续冲。BCEHS 要求至少冲十五分钟，考纲的烧伤规程是冷却十五到二十分钟。冲完要给病人保暖。眼睛只能用清水冲，绝不能用醋或小苏打。撑开眼睑，别让冲下来的水流进另一只眼。隐形眼镜冲不掉的话，冲一两分钟后暂停，把它取出来。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: burns and fluids
slides.body:
BC exam guidelines: Burn Management + Hypovolemia protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Expose and examine
  • Cool 15–20 min
  • High-flow O₂ if inhalation injury or SOB
  • Calculate BSA
  • Consider pain management
  • After cooling: dry, sterile, non-stick gauze

PCP adds

  • IV if indicated
  • Hypotensive: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Burns > 20% BSA → hypovolemia protocol
  • En route or if delayed; reassess every 500 mL
slides.say: Here's the Burn Management protocol from the BC exam guidelines. Every licence level exposes and examines, cools for fifteen to twenty minutes, gives high-flow oxygen for a suspected inhalation injury or shortness of breath, calculates the burned area, considers pain management, and applies a dry, sterile, non-stick dressing after cooling. The PCP adds the IV: start one if indicated, and if the patient is hypotensive, give twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres. Burns over twenty percent of body surface area, partial and full thickness, also meet the hypovolemia protocol, where the IV and fluids happen en route or during a delay, reassessing every five hundred millilitres.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 考纲里的烧伤处理流程。所有执照级别都要：暴露和检查；冷却十五到二十分钟；疑似吸入性损伤或气短时给高流量氧；计算烧伤面积；考虑镇痛；冷却后盖干的、无菌、不粘的敷料。PCP 多了静脉通路：有指征就开；病人低血压时，按每公斤二十毫升补液，最多两升。部分层加全层烧伤超过体表面积百分之二十，也符合低血容量流程：静脉和补液在途中或有延误时进行，每五百毫升复评一次。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Never delay transport for an IV; no repeated attempts if BP is OK
  • Avoid burned skin if you can, but it's not forbidden
  • A burned arm beats a leg; lines may be lost as tissue swells
  • Fluid creep: swelling threatens the airway and limbs
  • Older adults: pulmonary edema risk → listen to the lungs
  • Children: more fluid per kg, but check glucose
slides.say: Now the PCP watch-outs. An IV is never a reason to delay transport, and if the patient isn't clearly hypotensive, don't make repeated attempts on scene. Avoid burned skin if you can, but it isn't forbidden; a burned arm is better than a leg. Too much fluid, fluid creep, causes swelling that can threaten the airway and the limbs. Older adults can develop pulmonary edema, so listen to the lungs as you give fluid. Children need more fluid per kilogram, but they also run low on sugar faster, so check their blood glucose.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 要注意的事。开静脉永远不是耽误转运的理由；病人没有明显低血压的话，不要在现场反复穿刺。尽量避开烧伤的皮肤，但并不禁止；烧伤的手臂比腿好。补液过多，也就是液体蠕变，引起的水肿会威胁气道和肢体。老年人容易出现肺水肿，补液时要听肺。儿童每公斤需要的液体更多，但血糖也掉得更快，所以要测血糖。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Cooling: book says "several minutes" → BC 15–20 min
  • Parkland is textbook; BC hypotensive bolus: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • BC: burns > 20% BSA → hypovolemia protocol
  • Book's IO, morphine, fentanyl → not on the BC exam (BCEHS: opioids ACP; IO per D03)
  • Hypoglycemia: BGL < 4.0 mmol/L; IV dextrose is D10W only
  • EMRs have no IV access
slides.say: Let's line up the book and BC. The book only says cooling takes several minutes; BC says fifteen to twenty. The Parkland formula is textbook content; in BC, a hypotensive burn patient gets twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, and burns over twenty percent start the hypovolemia protocol. The book's morphine and fentanyl are not on the exam drug list, and the exam has no IO, or intraosseous, procedure. In BCEHS, those opioids are ACP drugs, and a PCP IO needs a hypovolemic arrest at twelve or older, or an ACP directing. The book says burned children may need sugar early; in BC, hypoglycemia means a blood glucose under four point zero, and the only IV dextrose is D10W. EMRs have no IV access, so the fluid work is yours.
slides.sayZh: 把书和 BC 对一下。书上只说冷却要「几分钟」；BC 规定十五到二十分钟。Parkland 公式是教材内容；在 BC，低血压的烧伤病人按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液，烧伤超过百分之二十就启动低血容量流程。书里的吗啡和芬太尼，都不在考试药物清单上；考纲也没有 IO（骨髓腔通路）操作。在 BCEHS，这些阿片类药是 ACP 用药；PCP 做 IO 则须是十二岁及以上的低血容量性心脏骤停，或有 ACP 指挥。书上说烧伤儿童可能早早需要补糖；在 BC，低血糖指血糖低于四点零，静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。EMR 没有静脉通路权限，所以补液的工作是你的。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Count partial + full thickness only; location matters as much as size
  2. Exam: cool 15–20 min, cool not cold; then dry sterile dressing, keep warm (BCEHS: 15 min, gel dressing)
  3. PCP: IV if indicated; low BP → 20 mL/kg, max 2 L; > 20% BSA → hypovolemia

Next: Chapter 24, Head and Face Injuries
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: count only partial- and full-thickness burns, and remember that location matters as much as size. Two: for the exam, cool for fifteen to twenty minutes with cool, not cold, water, then apply a dry, sterile, non-stick dressing and keep the patient warm. BCEHS cools for fifteen minutes and uses gel burn dressings. Three: as a PCP, start an IV if indicated. A hypotensive burn patient gets twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, and burns over twenty percent start the hypovolemia protocol. Next, Chapter twenty-four: head and face injuries. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，只算部分层和全层烧伤，并记住部位和面积同样重要。二，考试时，用凉而不冰的水冷却十五到二十分钟，然后盖干的、无菌、不粘的敷料，并给病人保暖；BCEHS 是冷却十五分钟，用凝胶烧伤敷料。三，作为 PCP，有指征就开静脉；低血压的烧伤病人按每公斤二十毫升、最多两升补液；烧伤超过百分之二十就启动低血容量流程。下一章是第二十四章：头面部损伤。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
